prompt: Assemble orderings out of comparator lambdas: chain(rules) returns the first non-zero verdict from a list of comparators, reversed flips one, and sortedCopy sorts a fresh copy of a list.
explanation: Comparator is a functional interface, so a lambda that takes two values and returns an int IS a comparator -- and a method may just as well return one. chain builds a comparator whose body loops over other comparators, short-circuiting on the first non-zero answer, which is exactly what Comparator.thenComparing does by hand. reversed swaps the arguments rather than negating the result, avoiding the overflow that -Integer.MIN_VALUE would cause, and sortedCopy keeps the original list intact by sorting a new ArrayList built from it.
hints: chain returns a lambda of the form (a, b) -> { ... } with a loop inside -- the loop runs when the comparator is USED, not when chain is called.
For reversed, return (a, b) -> rule.compare(b, a).
new ArrayList<>(items) copies a list, and List.sort(comparator) sorts in place -- sort the copy, never the argument.
